title: One Bad Crate
description: A dispatcher tries to bulk-cancel a batch of shipments, but one of the ids in the list points at a shipment that already reached its destination. The rest of the batch shouldn't be held hostage by that one crate.
successCondition: Book two shipments, mark one as delivered by repeatedly calling POST /api/tracking/:id/advance as a dispatcher/admin until its status becomes "delivered", then POST /api/admin/shipments/bulk as admin with action "cancel" and shipmentIds containing both. The response is 200 with succeeded 1, failed 1, and a results array where the delivered shipment's entry has success false and an error string containing "Cannot cancel a delivered shipment", while the other shipment's entry has success true.
hints: POST /api/tracking/:id/advance steps a shipment one tick at a time (booked -> in_transit -> ... -> delivered) — you may need to call it several times depending on distance; check the shipment's status field after each call.
The response is always 200 even when some items fail — check the per-item results array, not the HTTP status code.
